aboutUs.heroTitle: Learning, reimagined for every kind of mind
aboutUs.heroSubtitle: Learnigo is a play first learning platform built for dyslexic and neurodivergent learners — where reading, writing and speaking feel like an adventure, not a struggle.
aboutUs.paragraph: We believe every child learns differently, and that difference is something to celebrate, not fix. Learnigo turns lessons into short, encouraging rounds with audio support, playful visuals and instant positive feedback — so kids build real confidence, one star at a time.

english.title: English Kingdom
english.text: Stories, listening and speaking practice designed for dyslexia friendly reading.

maths.title: Maths Galaxy
maths.text: Bite sized number practice that turns tricky problems into fun little wins.

science.title: Science Lab
science.text: Curiosity driven activities that make discovery exciting, one experiment at a time.

care.title: Made With Care
care.text: Built alongside educators for dyslexic and neurodivergent learners.

playful.title: Playful & Positive
playful.text: Every round is short, encouraging, and celebrates progress instantly.

safe.title: Safe Space to Learn
safe.text: No red marks, no pressure — just gentle nudges and cheerful feedback.

language.title: Speaks Their Language
language.text: Available in 14 languages so every child feels at home.

progress.title: Progress That Shows
progress.text: Stars, streaks and a friendly dashboard keep the whole family in the loop.

settings.title: Play settings

sound.hapticsHintVibrate: This device has a vibration motor
sound.hapticsHintNone: No motor found — a deep sound pulse is used instead

vision.reducedMotionHint: No particles, no pulsing, no screen flashes
vision.highContrastHint: Stronger outlines and a darker background behind targets
vision.captionsHint: Keeps the written prompt on screen alongside the voice
vision.mirrorViewHint: On = like a mirror, which is what almost every child expects
vision.showSkeletonHint: Draws the tracked hand and body outline

body.seatedHint: Keeps every target inside a seated reach
body.extraTimeHint: Multiplies every response window. Speed is never the point.
body.dwellMsHint: How long a fingertip rests on a target to choose it. Longer helps a shaky hand.
body.handSwapHintWithDate: Reach set up {{date}}. Turn this on if the game names the wrong hand.
body.handSwapHintNoDate: Turn this on if the game names the wrong hand. Ask the child to raise their right hand to check.

help.promptModeHint: How much help the game gives. Adaptive fades it as the child succeeds without it.
help.adaptiveStageHelpBody: Starts at demonstration and fades one stage after five of six correct answers given without the prompt. Steps back after two errors.
help.difficultyModeHint: Adaptive moves one demand at a time — target size, then number of choices, then distractor similarity. Fixed holds one journey level instead.
help.fixedLevelHint: Plays and scores every round at this level, whichever the child picks. A pass is recorded as a real clear.
help.unlockAllHint: For a child already past level 1, or to probe one level. Clearing still has to be earned.
help.stageGSuffix: A high score here is not evidence the skill generalised; that has to be checked away from the screen.

data.telemetryHint: Trial-by-trial accuracy, thinking time, movement time and reach quality. Only numbers — never any video or image.
data.showMetricsHint: Frame rate, detection time and camera lag, for setting up a session
data.cameraNote: Camera frames are processed on this device only. No frame is stored or uploaded, by us or by anyone else.
data.eraseProfile: Erase this child's profile and history
data.eraseConfirm: Erase the reach calibration, capability profile, level progress, points and every stored round?

insights.title: Progress & analysis
insights.dashboardTitle: This child's full learning dashboard, with a summary of this report linked in
insights.exportTitle: Download the trial-level data as CSV

empty.title: Nothing recorded yet
empty.body: Play a camera game and every turn is measured here — what was understood, how much help was needed, how long thinking took and how long moving took, each kept separate.

gotIdea.label: Got the idea
gotIdea.hint: Correct, plus right answer reached imprecisely or late. This is the understanding number.

onTheirOwn.label: On their own
onTheirOwn.hint: Correct with no highlight and no demonstration. The independence number.

thinkingTime.label: Thinking time
thinkingTime.hint: Median time from the instruction to the first intentional movement. A decision measure, not a motor one.

movingTime.label: Moving time
movingTime.hint: Median time from starting to move to touching the target. A motor measure, kept out of accuracy entirely.

reachDirectness.label: Reach directness
reachDirectness.hint: Straight-line distance ÷ the path the hand actually travelled. 100% is perfectly direct.

noRounds.title: No recorded rounds
noRounds.body: The trial-level data has been erased, so there is nothing to analyse here. Levels and points are stored separately and are still on the Journey tab. Play a round and these tabs fill up again.

whereTheyAre.title: Where they are
whereTheyAre.note: Levels cleared per group. The group a child is progressing in is the developmental domain they are actually working on, which is more useful than a total.

levelPerGame.title: Level reached, per game
levelPerGame.noteStuckSingular: {{count}} game played several times with nothing cleared — shown first. That level is asking for something this child cannot do yet.
levelPerGame.noteStuckPlural: {{count}} games played several times with nothing cleared — shown first. That level is asking for something this child cannot do yet.
levelPerGame.noteOk: Games played, most progressed first. A game played repeatedly with nothing cleared would appear at the top.

journeyTab.serverRowNote: {{count}} games with journey data on the server, across all this child's devices

howEarned.title: How that progress was earned
howEarned.note: Three different claims, deliberately not added together.

demonstrated.name: Demonstrated
demonstrated.text: The child met the level's comprehension bar. This is evidence.

effort.name: Given for persistence
effort.text: Three attempts that landed close to the bar. The level opened anyway, so one badly-matched level cannot end a child's use of the app — but it is not evidence they met it.

implied.name: Inferred
implied.text: Credited because a harder level was cleared, and each level is at least as demanding as the one below. Never observed directly.

remote.name: Restored from another device
remote.tooltip: Restored from this child's other device. The payload carries which levels cleared but not how, so this device has no evidence for them.
remote.text: Came back from the server, which records which levels cleared but not how. No evidence on this device.

howEarned.footer: None of these three is evidence of real-world transfer. A cleared level means the child did the task on a screen.

trend.title: Understanding and independence over time
trend.note: Two lines, because they move separately. A child can understand more while still needing the same amount of help.

overviewTab.trendPlaceholder: Play on a second day to see a trend here.

promptMix.title: How much help was needed
promptMix.note: Share of turns at each prompt stage. Fading from A towards D is the goal; stage G is checked off-screen by an adult and can never be awarded by the game.

gamesPlayed.title: Games played
gamesPlayed.note: Accuracy and independence per game, most-played first.

overviewTab.serverRowNote: {{count}} games recorded on the server across all devices

profile.title: Capability profile
profile.note: A running estimate per functional domain, from in-game behaviour only. Domains with fewer than three turns are hidden because the estimate would be noise.

domainsTab.profilePlaceholder: Play a few more games — at least three domains need data before a profile means anything.

weakest.title: Weakest first
weakest.note: Accuracy on turns tagged with each domain. The lowest bars are where the next session is worth spending.

promptPerGame.title: Prompt stage per game
promptPerGame.note: Where the child currently sits on the help ladder in each activity.

leftRight.title: Left and right
leftRight.note: Same task, each hand. A consistent gap in accuracy or directness is worth an adult's attention; a gap in speed alone often is not.

motorTab.dominantHandNote: Spontaneously preferred hand: {{hand}} ({{left}} left / {{right}} right reaches)

rhythm.title: Rhythm timing
rhythm.note: Steadiness is the standard deviation of the timing error and is the meaningful number — a constant offset is just an offset, and part of it is camera lag, which is measured and subtracted per session.

motorTab.rhythmPlaceholder: Play Rhythm Reach a couple of times to see timing here.

reachEnvelope.title: Reach envelope
reachEnvelope.note: The calibrated play space every game places targets inside.

motorTab.reachPlaceholderSuffix: — until then targets use a generic envelope and a restricted reach will look like poor accuracy.

practised.title: Life skills practised
practised.note: Grouped by the real-world skill each game transfers to, not by the game.

routine.title: Routine steps done unaided
routine.note: For sequence games like handwashing: how many steps went in the right order without a reminder. 3/7 → 5/7 → 6/7 is what real progress looks like.

lifeTab.routinePlaceholder: Play a routine game (washing, dressing, crossing the road) to see this.

transfer.title: Real-world transfer
transfer.note: The stage the game cannot award.

lifeTab.transferP1Bold: Stage G is checked by a person, away from the screen.
lifeTab.transferP1Rest: A child who can pick the toothbrush out of five pictures has not yet been shown to pick up the actual toothbrush in the actual bathroom.
lifeTab.transferP2: Use the routine scores above to decide when a skill is worth trying for real, then record what happened in your own notes — this app deliberately does not claim to have measured it.

footer.disclaimer: These are descriptions of what happened in the games, not clinical measures. A high score is not evidence that a skill transfers off the screen — that has to be checked in real life.

B.name: Guided practice

F.name: Real-life framing

G.name: Real-world transfer

setup-space.title: Set Up My Space
setup-space.how: Five easy stretches so every game lands exactly where you can reach. Do this once, first.

ball-pop.title: Ball Pop
ball-pop.how: Balloons appear in your reach — pop each one before it floats away.

number-hunt.title: Whole-Body Number Hunt
number-hunt.how: Numbers appear high, low, left and right. Use your whole body to reach them.

two-hand-catch.title: Two-Hand Catch
two-hand-catch.how: Two shapes, one for each hand. Touch them both at the same moment.

cross-the-middle.title: Cross the Middle
cross-the-middle.how: Your left hand fetches things on the right, and the other way round.

left-or-right.title: Left or Right?
left-or-right.how: "Touch it with your LEFT hand." Knowing which is which.

reach-near-far.title: Reach Near & Far
reach-near-far.how: Some things are close, some are right at the edge of your reach.

find-touch-colour.title: Find & Touch
find-touch-colour.how: "Touch the blue one." Colours first, then shapes and numbers.

find-shape.title: Find the Shape
find-shape.how: "Touch the triangle." Ten shapes, some easy to mix up.

read-and-find.title: Read & Find
read-and-find.how: The word CIRCLE appears. Touch the circle. Nothing is read aloud.

listen-and-find.title: Listen & Find
listen-and-find.how: A voice says the word. Nothing is written. Find what you hear.

search-the-room.title: Search the Room
search-the-room.how: One right answer hiding among lots of very similar ones.

big-or-small.title: Big or Small?
big-or-small.how: Bigger, smaller, more, fewer — the comparison words.

above-or-below.title: Above or Below?
above-or-below.how: "Touch the cat above the box." Space words, in space.

which-animal.title: Which Group?
which-animal.how: "Touch the farm animal." Sorting the world into kinds.

go-no-go-animals.title: Pets Only!
go-no-go-animals.how: Touch the pets. Leave the wild animals completely alone.

rule-switch.title: Rule Switch
rule-switch.how: Touch the animals… then suddenly the rule changes to vehicles.

safe-or-not.title: Safe Hands
safe-or-not.how: Touch what is safe to hold. Never touch what is not.

red-light-green-light.title: Red Light, Green Light
red-light-green-light.how: Move when it is green. Freeze completely when it turns red.

traffic-light-body.title: Traffic Light Game
traffic-light-body.how: Green walk, amber get ready, red freeze — like a real crossing.

wait-for-it.title: Wait For It
wait-for-it.how: The star is there — but do not touch it until it turns green.

calm-movement.title: Calm Movement
calm-movement.how: Keep moving, but keep it gentle. Not too still, not too wild.

fast-vs-slow.title: Fast or Slow
fast-vs-slow.how: Move your arms fast, then very slowly. Choosing your own speed.

vanishing-target.title: Vanishing Target
vanishing-target.how: A letter flashes up, then disappears. Which one was it?

simon-reach.title: Simon Reach
simon-reach.how: Watch the order the shapes light up in, then copy it exactly.

copy-the-pattern.title: Copy the Pattern
copy-the-pattern.how: Red, blue, yellow, red — watch the colour pattern, then repeat it.

repair-the-alphabet.title: Repair the Alphabet
repair-the-alphabet.how: A, B, ?, D — find the letter that fell out.

whats-missing.title: What's Missing?
whats-missing.how: Look in the school bag, then say what went missing.

grocery-mission.title: Grocery Mission
grocery-mission.how: "Get milk, an apple and bread." Hold the list in your head and fetch them.

phonics-reach.title: Phonics Reach
phonics-reach.how: You hear /b/. Reach for the letter that makes that sound.

beginning-sound.title: Beginning Sound
beginning-sound.how: "Which one starts with /k/?" Reach the cat.

word-builder.title: Word Builder
word-builder.how: Spell C-A-T by reaching the letters in order.

word-and-picture.title: Word & Picture
word-and-picture.how: The word SUN appears. Touch the picture that matches.

air-writing.title: Air Writing
air-writing.how: Write letters and numbers in the air with your finger.

number-match.title: How Many?
number-match.how: The number 5 appears. Touch the group with five things in it.

count-and-collect.title: Count & Collect
count-and-collect.how: "Collect four apples." Counting while you move.

money-shop.title: Money Shop
money-shop.how: The apple costs 30c. Pick the coins that pay for it.

sentence-order.title: Sentence Order
sentence-order.how: I / want / water — put the words in the right order.

rhythm-reach.title: Rhythm Reach
rhythm-reach.how: Touch the shape exactly on every beat. Perfect, great, close — all count.

mirror-me.title: Mirror Me
mirror-me.how: Copy the position the little figure is holding.

copy-my-gesture.title: Copy My Gesture
copy-my-gesture.how: Wave, thumbs up, point, open palm — the gestures people use.

personal-space.title: My Space Bubble
personal-space.how: Keep your body inside your bubble — then step right outside it.

trace-the-road.title: Trace the Road
trace-the-road.how: Drive your finger along the winding road without going off it.

shape-drawing.title: Shape Drawing
shape-drawing.how: Draw a circle, a square, a star — in the air.

ar-maze.title: Finger Maze
ar-maze.how: Find your way through the maze without touching the walls.

pinch-and-write.title: Pinch & Write
pinch-and-write.how: Pinch your finger and thumb to hold the pen, then write. Like a real pencil grip.

handwashing.title: Wash My Hands
handwashing.how: Tap on, wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry — all in the right order.

toothbrushing.title: Brush My Teeth
toothbrushing.how: Every step of brushing, in order.

getting-dressed.title: Getting Dressed
getting-dressed.how: Underwear, top, trousers, socks, shoes — order matters.

morning-routine.title: Morning Routine
morning-routine.how: Wake up, toilet, wash, dress, breakfast, bag.

pack-my-bag.title: Pack My School Bag
pack-my-bag.how: Take what you need for school. Leave the rest behind.

sort-the-groceries.title: Sort the Groceries
sort-the-groceries.how: Pinch to pick it up, then drop it in the fridge, freezer or cupboard.

laundry-sort.title: Laundry Sort
laundry-sort.how: Lights in one basket, darks in the other.

tidy-the-room.title: Tidy the Room
tidy-the-room.how: Everything goes back to the room it belongs in.

where-does-it-go.title: Where Does It Go?
where-does-it-go.how: Milk — fridge, freezer or cupboard? Touch the right one.

hot-sharp-safe.title: Hot, Sharp or Safe
hot-sharp-safe.how: Which one gets hot? Which one is sharp? Which one is safe?

safe-or-unsafe.title: Safe or Not Safe?
safe-or-unsafe.how: Sometimes touch the safe thing, sometimes point out the dangerous one.

crossing-the-road.title: Crossing the Road
crossing-the-road.how: Stop, look, listen, wait, cross — the order that keeps you safe.

clean-or-dirty.title: Needs Washing?
clean-or-dirty.how: Socks go in the wash. Books do not. Which one needs washing?

my-day.title: My Whole Day
my-day.how: Wash, dress, pack, pay, cross the road, listen to the teacher, ask for help. The whole day, in one go.
my-day.opening: Good morning! Let us get through the day together.
my-day.openingSay: Good morning. Let us get through the day together.

dress.title: Get dressed
dress.say: Now get dressed. What goes on first?

pack.title: Pack your bag
pack.say: Pack what you need for school.

pay.title: Pay for lunch
pay.say: You need coins for your lunch.

road.title: Cross the road
road.say: Time to cross the road. Green means walk, red means freeze.

classroom.title: Listen to the teacher
classroom.say: The teacher has three things for you to do.

help.title: Ask for help
help.say: You cannot find your pencil. What can you do?

follow-two.title: Follow Two Things
follow-two.how: "Touch the star, then clap your hands." Two things, in order.

follow-three.title: Follow Three Things
follow-three.how: "Touch the 3, clap, then touch the blue one." Three, in order.

emotion-match.title: How Would They Feel?
emotion-match.how: Something happens in the story. Which feeling fits?

what-should-i-do.title: What Should I Do?
what-should-i-do.how: "Someone dropped their pencil." What is the kind thing to do?

ask-for-help.title: Ask For Help
ask-for-help.how: The jar will not open. Choosing to ask is the answer.

stay-safe-choices.title: Stop, Think, Do
stay-safe-choices.how: Something has gone wrong. Stop, think, then choose what to do.

time-of-day.title: When Do We?
time-of-day.how: Toothbrush — morning or night? Matching things to times of day.

coin-names.title: Which Coin?
coin-names.how: "Which one is fifty cent?" Naming and finding money.
